finalMessage:
I've added the Tournament mode, and every check passes: type check, 173 unit tests, all 84 browser tests (77 existing plus 7 new) and Prettier. One caveat on that: this machine has Node 22.23 and Playwright's bundled headless Chromium, not the named combination the README asks for (Node 26.12.1, Chromium 156), so the runs were without `NEON_PAIRS_NAMED_COMBINATION`. I pointed the tests at that browser with `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=[machine-path] The README still says the checks passed on the named combination, and that hasn't been re-checked for this change. Nothing is committed.

**How it works**
- **Opening it:** Tournament sits between New Game and Restart. The setup screen has the Players select (4 or 8), inputs labelled Player 1 to Player 8, Start tournament and Back to game. Names must not be empty, must differ from each other ignoring letter case, and can be up to 32 characters. A bad name shows a message and puts the cursor in that input.
- **Pairings:** round one pairs Player 1 with 2, 3 with 4, and so on, in the order typed. Later matches take the winners of earlier ones.
- **Deals:** each match gets its own random deal at the grid size free play had selected. Both players in a match get the same deal.
- **Turns:** "Now playing: NAME" is shown with Start turn. When a game ends, Next turn or Next match appears, and Leave tournament is always available. The bracket shows each match's players, moves, time (m:ss) and "Winner: NAME". The end screen shows "Champion: NAME" and Back to game.
- **Saving:** Export tournament and Load tournament, with the Tournament JSON box, are on every Tournament screen. Finished tournaments are kept in browser storage (key `neon-pairs.tournaments.v1`) and shown in Past tournaments, newest first.
- **Project rules:** I followed the rules the existing tests enforce: files under 200 lines, every export used somewhere, no unsafe type casts, yes/no checks named as questions, spacing on the 0/4/6/8/12/16/24/32 scale, and 44px tap targets.

**Choices I made where you didn't specify — easy to change**
- **Ties:** fewer moves wins; equal moves go to the faster time; an exact tie goes to whoever played first.
- **Leaving:** Leave tournament goes back to free play. A tournament left early is not added to Past tournaments.
- **Reloading:** an unfinished tournament isn't saved, so a reload goes back to free play. To keep one, use Export tournament.
- **List size:** Past tournaments keeps the 50 most recent.
- **Bests:** tournament games don't change your saved best moves, and the Best stat is hidden during a turn.
- **What Export saves:**
  - On the setup screen it saves the names typed so far.
  - During a turn it also saves that player's game; after loading, the game continues when they press Start turn.
  - Text that isn't a valid tournament shows "Invalid tournament." and changes nothing.

**Changes to existing code and tests**
- The new button adds a keyboard stop between New Game and Restart, so I updated the existing accessibility test and its fixture to expect it (`tests/accessibility.e2e.test.ts`, `tests/accessibility.fixture.json`, `tests/accessibility-fixture.ts`). The other existing browser tests pass without changes.
- The game now starts from a new app component in `src/game/App.tsx` that switches between free play and the tournament screen. The session test page (`art/session/session-harness.tsx`) renders that instead of the game directly.
- I pulled the page header, the board help text and the game's live message area into small shared components (`src/game/Masthead.tsx`, `src/game/board/BoardHelp.tsx`, `src/game/status/GameResult.tsx`). In `src/game/status/GameStatus.tsx`, passing `best={null}` now hides the Best stat.
- I moved the spacing check into `tests/spacing-scale.ts` so the tournament layout test can reuse it.
- I added a test to `tests/timer-lifecycle.e2e.test.ts` that leaving mid-turn stops that turn's timer.

The README has a new Tournament section.

Files are in the project:
- `src/game/tournament/` — all the new tournament code and its unit tests
- `tests/tournament.e2e.test.ts`
- `tests/tournament-transfer.e2e.test.ts`
- `tests/tournament-layout.e2e.test.ts`
- `tests/tournament-fixture.ts`

finalMessage:
Tournament mode is built and all checks pass: typecheck, 161 unit and source-audit tests, and 88 browser journeys (the 77 existing ones plus 11 new). One caveat on the browser results: they ran on Node 22.23.4 with Chromium 156 revision 1243 (Playwright's expected 1248 wasn't installed). That is not the named combination, so the README's tested-combination record is unchanged.

**How it works**
- **Opening it:** the Tournament button sits between New Game and Restart. It switches to the Tournament screen, and the solo game keeps its progress with its clock stopped until you come back.
- **Setup:** a Players select (4 or 8), inputs labelled Player 1 to Player 8, Start tournament, and Back to game. Names are trimmed, inner spaces collapsed and Unicode normalized. A name outside 2 to 20 characters shows "Use 2 to 20 characters.", and a repeat (ignoring case) shows "Each name must be different."
- **Pairings and boards:** seeds follow entry order. Four players open 1v4 and 2v3; eight open 1v8, 4v5, 3v6 and 2v7. Rounds are Quarterfinal on 4x4, Semifinal on 6x6 and Final on 8x8. Every match gets its own board code, chosen when the tournament starts.
- **Turns:**
  - Each turn shows "Round: NAME" and the match, such as "Semifinal 1: Ada against Dev". The status line shows "Now playing: NAME".
  - Start turn deals the board.
  - A finished game shows Next turn, or Next match when the match is over.
  - Fewer moves wins, then less active time, then the higher seed.
- **Leave tournament** asks first in a native dialog with Keep playing (focused, also what Escape does) and Leave.
- **Bracket:** a table with Match, Player, Moves, Time and Winner.
- **End:** when the final ends, the heading becomes "Champion: NAME" with Back to game.
- **Export and Load:** every screen has the Tournament JSON box. The export has a `"format": "neon-pairs/tournament"` field, a whole-number version and alphabetical keys. A bad load shows "Unknown field: NAME." for the first extra field, or "Invalid tournament." otherwise, and keeps your draft.
- **Past tournaments:** finished tournaments are saved under `np3:tournaments`, newest 10 kept, and appear on the setup and champion screens after reload. If storage is blocked, that table says "Progress won't be saved on this device." A corrupt saved value reads as empty and is left alone until the next save.
- **Solo records:** tournament games never change the saved board size or best scores. The browser test checks the stored preferences are byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Choices I made that you may want to revisit** (also saved in `.agents/memory/emerging/tournament-open-choices.md`):
- Load tournament replaces an unfinished tournament without the leave dialog, the same way Load snapshot works today.
- Exporting mid-game leaves the unfinished game out, so loading that export restarts the current player's turn on the same deal.
- The final goes straight to the champion screen; there's no Next match after it.
- The solo screen now has a visible "Solo game" heading, so Back to game has somewhere to put focus as the focus policy requires.
- I left the spec version at 2.2. Adding a mode may deserve 2.3 and release notes.
- Snapshot import still says "Invalid snapshot." for an unknown field, although the import-safety policy asks for "Unknown field: NAME." there too. That was out of scope.

**Changes outside the new feature**
- Two existing browser tests needed updates because of the new button and clock behaviour: the accessibility journey has one more tab stop, and the timer-lifecycle tests now share a counting helper.
- Shared game code was adjusted so solo and tournament play use the same turn logic and clock: `session.ts`, `use-session-clock.ts` (now able to pause while its screen is hidden), `use-game.ts`, `fresh-board.ts`, `GameStatus.tsx` (Best is optional), `Controls.tsx` and `game.css`.
- `npm run format:check` still warns about 214 Markdown files. That count is the same before my change; all code files pass.
- Nothing is committed.

**Files**
- New spec: `the project/docs/competition/competition-tournament.md`.
- Updated docs: 23 pages under `docs/` (competition, interface policies, persistence, sharing, architecture) plus the root `README.md`, wherever they said the tournament didn't exist yet.
- Feature code: `the project/src/game/tournament/`.
- Wiring: `the project/src/game/Game.tsx`.
- New browser tests: `the project/tests/tournament.e2e.test.ts`, `tournament-contract.e2e.test.ts` and `tournament-layout.e2e.test.ts`, with the helper `tournament-fixture.ts`.

finalMessage:
Tournament mode is working in the project. Type check passes, all 158 unit and source-audit tests pass, and all 84 browser tests pass through `npm run test:e2e`. 77 of those were already there; 7 are new. That run used Node 22.23.4 and Chrome for Testing 153, because the project's named Node 26 and Chromium 156 setup isn't on this machine, so it isn't the official record. I didn't commit anything.

**What players get**
- **Opening it:** a Tournament button sits right after New Game. It switches to the Tournament screen and moves focus to its "Tournament" heading.
- **Setup:** a Players select (4 or 8), fields labelled Player 1–8, and Start tournament. Names are trimmed, inner spaces collapsed and Unicode-normalized. A name outside 2–20 characters shows "Use 2 to 20 characters."; a repeat in any capitalization shows "Each name must be different."
- **Bracket and boards:** seeds follow entry order (1v4, 2v3; or 1v8, 4v5, 3v6, 2v7). "Round: NAME" shows while a round is played. Quarterfinals use 4x4 boards, semifinals 6x6 and the final 8x8. Both players in a match get the same deal, and no two matches share one.
- **Turns:** "Now playing: NAME" goes through the page's single status area. Start turn shows the board and focuses the first card. After a game, Next turn or Next match appears and the board hides at the handoff.
- **Winning a match:** fewer moves wins, then lower play time, then the higher seed.
- **Results:** a "Bracket" table shows each player's moves and time and each match's winner. At the end "Champion: NAME" appears with a Back to game button.
- **Leave tournament:** asks first in a dialog with "Keep playing" (focused, and Escape does the same) and "Leave".
- **Saved records:** tournament games never change the saved board size or best scores. Finished tournaments are kept on the device, newest 10, and shown in a "Past tournaments" table. Unreadable saved data shows as an empty list and is left alone until the next save. If storage is blocked, the screen says "Progress won't be saved on this device."
- **Export and load:** every Tournament view has Export tournament, Load tournament and a Tournament JSON box. An unrecognised field shows "Unknown field: NAME."; anything else wrong shows "Invalid tournament." Either way the current tournament stays.

**Choices you may want to change** (the request didn't settle these):
- **End of the final:** the champion appears straight away; there is no Next match button after the final. "Champion: NAME" is added to the last game's result in the same status message.
- **Single status area:** "Now playing" and "Champion" appear only there. The first result of a turn replaces "Now playing", so it isn't shown for the whole turn. Load errors also appear next to the JSON box, so that text shows twice on the page.
- **Leaving the normal game:** pressing Tournament during an unfinished game asks the same Keep playing / Leave question first. Back to game starts a fresh deal at the saved size.
- **Export before starting:** Export on the setup view writes a new tournament with fresh deals for the typed names. Loading a finished tournament doesn't add it to Past tournaments.
- **Button names clash:** Playwright's default, non-exact match on the dialog's "Leave" button also finds "Leave tournament". The words come from the project's dialog rule and your request, so I kept both.

**Changes to existing behaviour and tests**
- I updated the keyboard accessibility test (`tests/accessibility.e2e.test.ts`), because the new button adds one Tab stop.
- The deal buttons no longer wrap their text.
- The status bar can now hide the Best line; tournament games use that.
- `npm run format:check` already failed before my work, on 104 docs files. All the code passes.

**Where things are**
- New code is in `src/game/tournament/` (rules, bracket, names, export format and saved-records modules, each with tests, plus the hooks, components and CSS) and `src/game/board/BoardHelp.tsx`. Existing files I changed include `src/game/Game.tsx` and `src/game/session/session.ts`.
- New tests: `tests/tournament.e2e.test.ts` (a full four-player tournament), `tests/tournament-controls.e2e.test.ts`, `tests/tournament-fixture.ts`, plus a Tournament-screen spacing check in `tests/spacing.e2e.test.ts`.
- Docs: a new spec page `docs/competition/tournament.md`, linked from `docs/README.md`, with small updates to four other docs. `README.md` gets a usage paragraph and a note recording this test run.

finalMessage:
Tournament mode is built and working. Type checking, all 156 unit tests and all 88 browser journeys pass (77 existing, 11 new). One caveat on that: this machine has Node 22.23.4 with Chrome for Testing 153, not the project's named Node 26.12.1 / Chromium 156 combination, so the README's tested-combination record doesn't cover this run. Nothing is committed; the changes are in the working tree.

**How it works**
- **Opening it:** the Tournament button sits between New Game and Restart. Opening it replaces the main area and moves focus to the screen's "Tournament" heading. Back to game returns focus to a new "Solo game" heading. The solo game keeps its state while you're away and its clock doesn't run.
- **Players:** a Players select (4 or 8) and inputs labelled Player 1–8. Start tournament tidies each name (trims it, collapses inner spaces, normalizes the Unicode) and then checks it. A name under 2 or over 20 characters shows "Use 2 to 20 characters." A repeat, ignoring case, shows "Each name must be different." Entries and focus stay put.
- **Bracket rules:** seeds follow entry order. Openings are 1v4, 2v3 for four players and 1v8, 4v5, 3v6, 2v7 for eight. "Round: Quarterfinal/Semifinal/Final" is shown, on 4x4, 6x6 and 8x8 boards. Every match gets its own deal, different from every other match, and both players play it.
- **Turns:** "Now playing: NAME" goes through the page's single live region. The board waits closed until Start turn, which moves focus to the board. When a game ends its board stays up and Next turn or Next match appears. After the final, "Champion: NAME" appears with Back to game.
- **Winner:** fewer moves wins. Equal moves go to the lower exact active time, not the displayed seconds, then to the higher seed.
- **Saved data:** tournament games never change the saved size or best scores. The in-tournament stats show Moves, Pairs and Time, without Best.
- **Bracket table:** captioned "Bracket", with Seed, Player, Moves and Time columns. Moves read like "18 moves", unplayed games "Not played", and the winner gets "(winner)".
- **Leave tournament:** opens a native dialog. Keep playing takes focus and Escape keeps playing. Leave goes back to player entry and saves nothing.
- **Past tournaments:** stored under `np3:tournaments`, newest first, keeping 10, as a table of entrants and champion. A damaged stored value is quietly treated as empty and left alone until the next save. If storage is blocked, finished tournaments stay for the visit and the screen shows "Progress won't be saved on this device."
- **Tournament JSON:** every Tournament screen has the box with Export tournament and Load tournament. Exports are tagged `neon-pairs/tournament`, version 1, with keys in alphabetical order. A bad load shows "Unknown field: NAME." for the first unknown field, otherwise "Invalid tournament.", and keeps both the current tournament and the draft.

**Decisions you may want to revisit**
- Leave tournament returns to the player-entry screen rather than straight to the solo game.
- Before a tournament starts, Export tournament describes the tournament the typed names would create, deals included. With invalid names it shows the name message instead.
- Loading a tournament resumes at its next unplayed game. A game that was mid-play when exported isn't included.
- Loading an already finished tournament shows its champion but doesn't add it to Past tournaments.
- I added a visible "Solo game" heading to the main screen so Back to game has somewhere to put focus, as the focus rules require.
- I added a C15 requirement to `docs/controls.md` for the button's placement.

**Changes to existing tests:** the existing accessibility test now tabs past the extra button. The spacing check moved into `tests/spacing-scale.ts` so the new tournament screens reuse it.

**Formatting:** `npm run format:check` already failed before my changes, on about 100 files in `docs/`. That includes several docs I edited, which I left unreformatted. All code, `README.md` and the new `docs/tournament.md` pass.

**Where things are** (all under `the project`):
- Tournament code: `src/game/tournament/`. Pure rules are in `rules.ts`, `names.ts`, `format.ts` and `past-tournaments.ts`, each with a test file beside it.
- Changed existing code: `src/game/Game.tsx`, `src/game/session/session.ts`, `src/game/session/use-session-clock.ts`, `src/game/session/use-game.ts`, `src/game/controls/Controls.tsx`, `src/game/status/GameStatus.tsx`, plus the new `src/game/board/BoardHelp.tsx`.
- New browser tests: `tests/tournament*.e2e.test.ts` and `tests/tournament-fixture.ts`.
- Docs: new `docs/tournament.md`. Updated: `docs/README.md`, `controls.md`, `architecture.md`, `acceptance.md`, `source-layout.md`, the `competition-*` pages, the related policy pages and the project `README.md`.
